fields.v: Madduru, P. R. (2026). When Agents Implement Systems: A Case Study in Defects, Detection, and Evaluation Rigor. arXiv:2609.01985v1 [cs.AI], 2 Sep 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2609.01985v1 [cs.AI], marked 'Preprint', 5 pages; no venue stated
Amazon.com (industry; single author)

Evaluates — observational single-session case study of one LLM coding agent implementing a multi-component data system against a detailed pre-existing specification: catalog of five agent-introduced defects (constraint violated, detection method), plus an external benchmark (HotpotQA) evaluation of the specified retrieval-filtering trade-off
No named SDD approach: spec-directed implementation by 'Claude, operated via a CLI coding tool' against a pre-existing design document. Agent, model and tool versions: Not stated

Pre-existing design document fixing storage technologies, schema, entity-resolution algorithm and retrieval-filtering strategy (interaction-design details left open); session artefacts used as data: code diffs, test output, screenshots, timing

Specification given in advance -> agent implements end to end in one extended session (graph store, filtered vector index, async ingestion pipeline, visualization client) -> defects diagnosed and fixed by the agent proactively or after user-reported symptoms -> post-hoc categorisation of defects; separate retrieval ablation on HotpotQA
User reports symptoms during development and use (e.g. latency, client crash); human caught an uncatalogued re-render inefficiency through interactive testing; no planned review gates described
Full implementation from a specification document (specification-to-code in one session); not a named workflow

Not classifiable (authors' wording: 'detailed pre-existing specification', 'spec-directed implementation', 'design document'; the spec is fixed before implementation, closest to spec-first, but no lifecycle of the spec is described)

rev.why: The design document is fixed before implementation and directs it (spec-first behaviour), but the paper says nothing about what happens to the spec afterwards; 'not classifiable' vs 'spec-first' is a judgement

A pre-existing design document fixed storage, schema, entity-resolution algorithm and retrieval strategy before implementation and directed it (p. 2), which is spec-first behaviour; the paper says nothing about whether the spec was kept or updated afterwards, so 'not classifiable' vs 'spec-first' is a judgement.

A pre-existing design document fixed storage, schema, entity-resolution algorithm and retrieval strategy before implementation and directed it (p. 2), which is spec-first behaviour; the paper says nothing about whether the spec was kept or updated afterwards, so 'not classifiable' vs 'spec-first' is a judgement.

fields.warn: O design document é fixado antes da implementação (p. 2), mas o artigo não diz se foi mantido depois. Decide entre spec-first e not classifiable.

The paper mentions only 'a user-reported symptom' (p. 2), 'user-observed latency' (Table 1) and 'a human caught this' (p. 4); it never says who operated the agent or their experience. That it was the single author is an inference.

Qualitative: where agent autonomy succeeded (structural fixes in two of five defects) vs needed human correction; unverified performance claim by the agent (fix not re-measured on the regression input)

Manual: post-hoc logging of defects from session artefacts (diffs, test output, screenshots, timing), no protocol decided in advance. Retrieval: automatic script (cosine similarity, recall against gold supporting-fact labels, exact sign test)

(1) Claude via a CLI coding tool (version and model not stated) + pre-existing specification: no success criterion stated by the authors; five defects introduced and fixed in one session (two diagnosed from a single symptom with a structural fix; one consistency defect reintroduced at a second call site; one performance fix claimed without re-measuring). Quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors. Cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors (no cost measured). Retrieval ablation (not an agent configuration): filtered vs unfiltered retrieval, recall@1 0.500 vs 0.420; recall@10 1.000 vs 0.845; exact match at k = 10 1.000 vs 0.690; sign test p < 10^-4 at every k

No comparison of agents or approaches. Only the retrieval ablation: filtered (candidates restricted to gold-titled paragraphs, a stand-in for entity identification) vs unfiltered similarity search, same corpus and embedder, 100 HotpotQA distractor-setting questions, k in {1, 3, 5, 10}, paired two-sided exact sign test

Agent: N/A. Retrieval: filtered recall reaches 1.0 from k = 3 (near-tautological by design); unfiltered recovers both gold paragraphs only 69% of the time at k = 10; differences significant at every k (p from 3x10^-5 to 3x10^-18)

N/A for agents. Retrieval ablation separated conditions but the author states the filtered ceiling follows from the design; gold-label substitution for entity identification limits generalisation to an automated pipeline

Single-session, single-agent case study; defect frequencies not claimed to generalise (including to smaller models); retrieval ablation substitutes gold entity labels and uses recall rather than HotpotQA's own metrics. Several defects had no static or type-level signature, arguing for execution-based evaluation of agentic systems work; the development loop had no mechanism forcing re-measurement against the regression a fix targeted or an external benchmark

Agent identified only as 'Claude, operated via a CLI coding tool'; model, tool and versions not stated. Defect log drawn from existing session artefacts, not a protocol decided in advance. Ablation script and results said to be retained alongside the paper's source; no repository link given; the system code is not released. Embedder not named. No pre-registration. Programming language not stated

rev.why: The author (Amazon) is not the vendor of Claude, but the CLI coding tool used is not named (p. 2); an Amazon author may have used an Amazon CLI that runs Claude, and §5 scores missing information as No. Yes kept as best value since the agent's model vendor is known to be independent.
